working_tree.note: The canonical run was executed during the integrity pass before its commit.

input.generation_procedure: Canonical JSON object with universe=[1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8], sizes=[2,3], and spectra equal to lexicographically ordered itertools.combinations(universe,size) for size 2 then 3; JSON serialized with sort_keys=True and separators=(',',':').

old_strict_order.limitation: Exactly one bridge can be represented as the unique lexicographic maximum, so triples with two or three self-sum-clean bridges are lost.

corrected_tied_signature.semantics: Every self-sum-clean bridge may tie weakly at the lexicographic maximum; partial and three-way ties are representable.

old_strict_order.stage: combinations with replacement of three spectra
three pairwise cross-sum checks avoid powers of two

corrected_tied_signature.stage: combinations with replacement of three spectra
three pairwise cross-sum checks avoid powers of two

direct_reconciliation_check.statement: The corrected-minus-old set is exactly the set of corrected cross-compatible triples with at least two self-sum-clean bridges; these and only these require a partial or three-way maximum tie unavailable to a strict permutation.

interpretation: Both finite counts are regression data only. The old count is incomplete; the corrected count confirms that the abstract conditions are insufficient. Neither count is evidence toward solving the conjecture, and zero graph-realizable survivors is vacuous because the n<=7 bridge library is empty.
